meta.name: Microsoft Security Operations Analyst (SC-200)
meta.notes: Initial pack: 10 questions covering Microsoft Defender XDR, Microsoft Defender for Cloud, Microsoft Sentinel, threat hunting, and incident response. | 2026-05-23 keyword-balance pass | 2026-06-01 +6 questions to unlock learning path | [scheduled-agent hardening pass 2026-06-11: full-pack rewrite — removed self-defeating distractor tails on sc-200-001/002/003/007/008/010, normalized option lengths so the correct option is never the longest or the only complete one, rebalanced positions to A/B/C/D = 4/4/4/4 with no more than two adjacent same-letter, moved why-wrong reasoning into explanations]

questions.question: A SOC running Microsoft Defender for Endpoint wants confirmed malicious files on developer workstations to be remediated automatically, but actions on production servers must wait for an analyst's approval. Which configuration achieves this with the least administrative effort?
options: Set the tenant automation level to Full and exclude all server device names from automated investigation runs in MDE settings
Disable automated investigation across the tenant and have analysts review and approve every remediation action manually for both fleets
Tag developer workstations as Tier 1 and add an indicator rule that blocks automated remediation against server FQDNs in the tenant
Create two device groups and set workstations to Full automatic remediation while servers require analyst approval for remediation actions
questions.explanation: Device groups in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint scope the automated investigation and remediation (AIR) level independently per group. Workstations set to Full let MDE auto-remediate confirmed threats, while a Semi-level on servers holds actions pending analyst approval. A single tenant-wide automation level cannot differ per device, and excluding servers from AIR entirely just stops investigation rather than gating remediation. Disabling AIR tenant-wide removes the automation benefit on the workstation fleet too. Indicator rules block specific IOCs and do not control AIR behavior on a device subset.
questions.domain: Mitigate threats using Microsoft Defender XDR

questions.question: Microsoft Defender for Identity raises a 'Suspected DCSync attack' alert pointing at a service account used by an authorized vulnerability scanner that legitimately replicates directory data. Which response prevents recurring false positives while preserving detection against unknown principals?
options: Close the alert as a true positive benign and mark the scanner account as a sensitive account so its activity gets closer monitoring
Disable the Suspected DCSync attack detection tenant-wide and rely on Sentinel KQL hunting against SecurityEvent for future detections
Close the alert as a false positive and exclude the scanner service account from the Suspected DCSync attack detection
Close the alert as a false positive and add the scanner service account to the Honeytoken exclusion list in Defender for Identity
questions.explanation: Defender for Identity supports per-detection exclusions; excluding the scanner from the Suspected DCSync attack detection silences the false positive while keeping the detector active for any other principal. Sensitive accounts heighten alerting rather than suppress it, so this makes the noise worse. Disabling the detection globally loses every real DCSync detection in the tenant. Honeytoken accounts are decoys that should never authenticate, so adding a real working account that performs legitimate replication will generate noise on every legitimate use rather than silence it.

questions.question: Users keep receiving phishing emails that link to freshly registered domains and slip past Exchange Online Protection. The tenant has Microsoft Defender for Office 365 Plan 2. Which feature, configured correctly, rewrites links in inbound mail and scans the destination at time of click?
options: An anti-phishing policy with mailbox intelligence-based impersonation protection enabled on every inbound recipient
A Safe Links policy applied to recipient mailboxes with URL rewriting and the Track user clicks option enabled
An Exchange mail flow rule that strips every HTML hyperlink from inbound email before delivery to user mailboxes
A Safe Attachments policy applied to all recipients with Dynamic Delivery enabled to detonate attachments in a sandbox
questions.explanation: Safe Links rewrites URLs in inbound mail and performs reputation and detonation checks at click time, catching domains weaponized after delivery. Mailbox intelligence-based impersonation protection guards against spoofed-sender lookalikes, not URL reputation on arbitrary linked domains. Stripping all hyperlinks at the transport layer breaks legitimate mail and is not a supported Microsoft control. Safe Attachments only inspects file payloads, not URLs.

questions.question: A team must prevent users on unmanaged devices from downloading files from SharePoint Online while still allowing browser-based read access. Which combination of Microsoft controls delivers exactly this requirement?
options: An Intune app protection policy on the SharePoint mobile app that prevents save-as operations to non-corporate storage on the device
An Entra Conditional Access policy that grants access only after MFA plus a Defender for Cloud Apps access policy that blocks the user session
A SharePoint Online unmanaged-devices policy that requires a managed device plus Microsoft Purview sensitivity labels marking the files as confidential
An Entra Conditional Access policy that routes the session through Defender for Cloud Apps plus a session policy that blocks downloads of sensitive files
questions.explanation: Conditional Access App Control routes the browser session through Defender for Cloud Apps' reverse proxy; a session policy can block downloads matching label, classification, or content-inspection criteria while keeping read access in the browser — exactly the requirement. Intune app protection covers mobile apps, not browser SharePoint. A Defender for Cloud Apps access policy makes a binary allow/block decision at sign-in and cannot enforce per-action controls like block-download-while-allow-view. The SharePoint unmanaged-devices policy blocks access entirely (or limits to view-only at a coarse level) and is not paired with sensitivity-aware enforcement.

questions.question: Microsoft Entra ID Protection raises a High user-risk score on an account whose credentials were observed in a leaked credential dump. Which automated response best matches Microsoft's recommended pattern for high user risk?
options: A Conditional Access policy that requires a secure password change when user risk is High, combined with enforced MFA on the account
A Conditional Access policy that requires multifactor authentication on every sign-in for every user in the tenant regardless of risk score
A Sentinel playbook that disables the affected user account in Active Directory the first time any user-risk signal is raised
An Intune device compliance rule that wipes the corporate workload from the user's device after three consecutive risky sign-ins
questions.explanation: User risk represents the probability that an identity itself is compromised (for example leaked credentials). Microsoft's recommended response is a secure password change combined with MFA, which both replaces the leaked secret and confirms presence. Blanket MFA on every sign-in is the sign-in-risk control and does not rotate the leaked password. Disabling on any signal is over-broad, ignores remediation paths, and breaks self-service MFA recovery flows. Wiping the device addresses an endpoint, not an identity that may already be used on other devices.

questions.question: An analyst opens an incident in the Microsoft Defender portal that correlates alerts from Defender for Endpoint, Defender for Office 365, and Defender for Identity. They want a single KQL query joining device, email, and identity telemetry. Which table set is correct?
options: WindowsEvent, AzureActivity, and AADNonInteractiveUserSignInLogs in the Log Analytics workspace bound to the Defender connector
SecurityEvent, OfficeActivity, and SigninLogs in the Microsoft Sentinel workspace via the Log Analytics query interface
DeviceProcessEvents, EmailEvents, and IdentityLogonEvents in the Microsoft Defender XDR advanced hunting schema
AlertEvidence and AlertInfo alone, since advanced hunting in the Defender portal exposes only those two alert-level tables
questions.explanation: The Microsoft Defender XDR advanced hunting schema exposes Device*, Email*, Identity*, App*, Cloud*, and Alert* tables and joins them across product telemetry inside the Defender portal — exactly what the analyst needs. WindowsEvent / AzureActivity / AADNonInteractiveUserSignInLogs live in Log Analytics for Sentinel, not in the Defender portal's hunting page. SecurityEvent / OfficeActivity / SigninLogs are also Sentinel-side Log Analytics tables. AlertEvidence and AlertInfo exist in advanced hunting but are a small subset; the raw activity tables provide the cross-product event detail the analyst is joining on.

questions.question: A multicloud team needs Microsoft Defender for Cloud to surface an attack path showing how an internet-facing AWS EC2 instance could pivot to a sensitive Azure SQL database. Which prerequisite must be satisfied for Cloud Security Explorer to render this path?
options: Enable the Defender CSPM (paid) plan on both the Azure subscription containing the SQL database and the AWS connector account
Enable the Foundational CSPM (free) plan in Defender for Cloud, since attack paths are part of the baseline posture features available to every subscription
Deploy the Azure Monitor Agent on the EC2 instance and stream Linux syslog into the Defender for Cloud workspace for cross-cloud correlation
Onboard the AWS account through the Microsoft Sentinel AWS data connector and write Sentinel analytics rules to map the cross-cloud path
questions.explanation: Cloud Security Explorer and attack path analysis are features of the paid Defender CSPM plan and require it enabled on each environment whose resources participate in the path — here both the Azure subscription and the AWS connector account. Foundational CSPM gives only free recommendations and secure score, not attack-path graphs. Defender CSPM uses agentless scanning, so the Azure Monitor Agent on EC2 is irrelevant. Sentinel ingests logs and runs detections but does not build the cross-cloud security graph that powers attack-path analysis.
questions.domain: Mitigate threats using Microsoft Defender for Cloud

questions.question: A team wants Microsoft Defender for Cloud to detect when a critical Azure Storage account starts receiving an unusual surge of access from a previously unseen IP, suggesting potential data exfiltration. Which workload protection plan must be enabled on the storage account's subscription?
options: Microsoft Defender for Resource Manager, which inspects management-plane API calls against the storage account and its role assignments
Microsoft Defender for Storage, which baselines access patterns and alerts on anomalies such as unfamiliar source IPs or odd request bursts
Microsoft Defender for Key Vault, since exfiltrated storage data would require key vault access to decrypt the underlying blob contents
Microsoft Defender for Servers Plan 2, since every storage account is backed by an underlying virtual machine serving the blob endpoints
questions.explanation: Defender for Storage monitors data-plane operations on storage accounts and generates alerts for anomalous access, suspicious IPs, malware uploads, and exposure events — exactly the scenario described. Defender for Resource Manager observes control-plane (ARM) operations like role-assignment changes, not data-plane request patterns. Defender for Key Vault watches key operations, which is unrelated to anomalous storage reads (and storage encryption is independent of whether attackers re-encrypt). Storage accounts are PaaS and do not expose a customer-managed VM that Defender for Servers could protect.

questions.question: A Microsoft Sentinel analyst needs a scheduled analytics rule that opens an incident when a single user fails sign-in to Microsoft Entra ID more than 50 times within any 10-minute window from any source IP. Which KQL pattern matches the requirement?
options: SecurityEvent | where EventID == 4625 | summarize FailedCount = count() by Account, bin(TimeGenerated, 10m) | where FailedCount > 50
SigninLogs | where ResultType == 0 | summarize SuccessCount = dcount(IPAddress) by UserPrincipalName | where SuccessCount > 50
AuditLogs | where Result == "failure" | summarize Bursts = count() by InitiatedBy_user_userPrincipalName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1h) | where Bursts > 50
SigninLogs | where ResultType != 0 | summarize FailedCount = count() by UserPrincipalName, bin(TimeGenerated, 10m) | where FailedCount > 50
questions.explanation: Microsoft Entra ID sign-in failures land in SigninLogs with a non-zero ResultType; binning by 10 minutes and thresholding above 50 per user implements the requirement directly. The SecurityEvent / EventID 4625 query captures on-prem Windows logon failures collected by the MMA or AMA agent, not Entra ID cloud sign-ins. The SuccessCount option filters ResultType == 0 (successful sign-ins) and counts distinct IPs, neither of which matches the requirement. AuditLogs holds directory-change events (group adds, role assignments) rather than authentication outcomes, and uses the wrong 1-hour window.

questions.question: A Microsoft Sentinel analytics rule fires hundreds of low-severity incidents per day. The SOC wants every newly created incident from that rule whose tactic is Discovery and whose status is New closed automatically, without writing custom code. Which Sentinel feature delivers this?
options: An automation rule triggered on incident creation with conditions on the rule name and the Discovery tactic and an action that closes the incident
A Microsoft Sentinel watchlist of suppressed rule names that the analytics rule consults via lookup() before generating any new incident
A Logic Apps playbook triggered on every newly created incident that calls the Sentinel API to evaluate the rule name and tactic and then close matches
An incident triage workbook that visualizes the noisy analytics rule and lets analysts mass-close matching incidents through a custom visualization
questions.explanation: Automation rules in Microsoft Sentinel run on incident creation or update with simple condition-and-action logic and can close incidents directly with no code — the lightweight built-in answer. Watchlists store reference data and cannot suppress an analytics rule's output before incident creation. A Logic Apps playbook could in principle close incidents, but it is unnecessary code for an action automation rules already do natively, and writing custom condition logic in Logic Apps adds maintenance the SOC explicitly wants to avoid. Workbooks are read-only dashboards, not enforcement tools.

questions.question: During an active incident, a SOC analyst confirms an endpoint is executing ransomware and must immediately cut off its network communication while preserving the machine for forensic investigation, all from the Microsoft Defender portal. Which Defender for Endpoint response action should they take?
options: Run an antivirus scan on the device and wait for the scan results before taking any further containment action
Isolate the device, which blocks its network connectivity while keeping it manageable from the Defender portal
Add the device to a restricted app execution policy so only Microsoft-signed binaries are allowed to run
Stop and quarantine the offending file across the organization using an indicator, then leave the device online
questions.explanation: Device isolation in Defender for Endpoint severs the machine's network connectivity to stop the ransomware spreading while keeping the Defender agent connected so analysts can investigate and later release it — meeting both requirements. Running a scan first delays containment while encryption and lateral movement continue. Restricting app execution limits new process launches but does not cut existing C2 or SMB connections the ransomware is already using. Stopping and quarantining the file via an indicator addresses that specific binary but leaves the device online and able to communicate.
questions.domain: Mitigate threats using Microsoft Defender XDR

questions.question: A SOC wants a threat-hunting query to run automatically every hour and raise an alert that becomes a Defender XDR incident whenever a rare LOLBin process executes with suspicious command-line arguments. Which Microsoft Defender XDR capability should they configure?
options: A device tag applied to hosts that have run LOLBins so they can be filtered in the device inventory by analysts
A saved advanced hunting query that analysts manually rerun each shift and triage by hand when results appear in the portal
A custom detection rule built from an advanced hunting query, scheduled to run and generate alerts and incidents
An indicator of compromise added for each known LOLBin executable so future executions are blocked outright on every device
questions.explanation: A custom detection rule wraps an advanced hunting KQL query and runs it on a schedule, automatically generating alerts that roll up into Defender XDR incidents — exactly the requested automation. Device tags only label hosts for filtering and raise no alerts. A saved query that analysts rerun manually provides no scheduled alerting and no incident creation. IoC indicators for LOLBin executables (powershell.exe, certutil.exe, mshta.exe) would block legitimate administrative use of those signed Windows binaries and cannot capture the command-line context that makes the execution suspicious.

questions.question: An organization onboards 200 servers to Microsoft Defender for Cloud and wants the SOC to investigate Defender for Servers alerts inside Microsoft Sentinel alongside its other security data, with bidirectional incident sync. Which integration should be configured?
options: Configure Azure Monitor diagnostic settings on each VM to send the Defender for Servers alerts directly into a custom Sentinel table
Export the Defender for Cloud alerts to a storage account nightly and import them into Sentinel with a scheduled Logic App workflow
Forward each Defender for Servers alert by email to a shared mailbox that Sentinel monitors via the mailbox data connector
Enable the Microsoft Defender for Cloud (Tenant-based) connector in Microsoft Sentinel to stream alerts and sync incidents bidirectionally
questions.explanation: The Microsoft Defender for Cloud connector in Microsoft Sentinel streams its security alerts into Sentinel and supports bidirectional incident synchronization, so investigations stay aligned across both products — exactly the requirement. Azure Monitor diagnostic settings on VMs carry resource diagnostics, not Defender for Cloud security alerts with incident sync. A storage-account export imported nightly adds hours of latency and provides no bidirectional incident sync. Emailing alerts to a mailbox is fragile, loses structured fields, and is not a supported alert-ingestion path.
questions.domain: Mitigate threats using Microsoft Defender for Cloud

questions.question: A Sentinel analyst must enrich incidents with up-to-date malicious IP indicators from a commercial feed delivered in STIX format over TAXII, so analytics rules can match logs against current threat intelligence. Which Sentinel capability ingests this feed?
options: A scheduled analytics rule that queries the vendor's public website hourly and parses the IP list out of the HTML response
A watchlist manually uploaded once as a CSV file and referenced by analytics rules using the _GetWatchlist function
The Threat Intelligence - TAXII data connector, which polls the TAXII server and imports STIX indicators into Sentinel
A Logic Apps playbook that runs after each incident to look up the IP against the vendor's interactive portal page
questions.explanation: The Threat Intelligence - TAXII data connector polls a TAXII server and imports STIX-formatted indicators into the ThreatIntelligenceIndicator table, keeping them current for analytics rules to match against logs — the supported pattern. Scraping a vendor website's HTML is brittle, unsupported, and bypasses STIX/TAXII entirely. A manually uploaded CSV watchlist is static and does not refresh from the feed. A post-incident playbook lookup enriches alerts after detection rather than supplying indicators that rules match against proactively.

questions.question: A Sentinel deployment ingests a high volume of verbose Azure Diagnostics logs that are rarely queried interactively but must be retained for a year for occasional compliance investigations, at the lowest cost. Which Log Analytics table plan should the analyst choose for that table?
options: The Auxiliary (or Basic) logs plan, which lowers ingestion cost for high-volume, infrequently queried data with longer retention
The Analytics (interactive) plan, since every table used in any KQL query must remain on the interactive tier in Log Analytics
The Sentinel summary-rules plan, which deletes the raw rows immediately after aggregating them each day to reduce storage
A separate Storage account export only, removing the data from Log Analytics entirely so it can never be queried again
questions.explanation: Auxiliary (and Basic) logs plans are designed for high-volume, infrequently queried data: they cut ingestion cost and support long retention for occasional compliance lookups, matching the requirement exactly. Keeping everything on the Analytics interactive tier is the most expensive option and is unnecessary for rarely queried data. There is no plan that deletes raw rows immediately after daily aggregation while still meeting the year-long retention need — summary rules summarize alongside the raw data, they do not replace it. Exporting only to a storage account removes the ability to query the data through Log Analytics during the compliance investigation.

questions.question: Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps generates an 'Impossible travel' alert for a user who signed in from two distant countries within minutes. The SOC wants to confirm whether this is a true compromise before disabling the account. Which investigation step in Defender for Cloud Apps is most appropriate first?
options: Immediately suspend the user in Microsoft Entra ID and reset their password before reviewing any related activity
Review the user's activity log and the related sign-in events to assess context such as IP, device, and prior behavior
Add both source IP addresses to the corporate firewall block list and close the alert as resolved without further review
Lower the impossible-travel detection sensitivity so the policy stops generating this category of alert for the user going forward
questions.explanation: Reviewing the user's activity log and the related sign-in events lets the analyst weigh context — IPs, devices, VPN use, and historical patterns — to decide whether the alert is a true compromise before acting, which is the correct first investigative step. Suspending and resetting the password immediately is a response action taken before confirming the verdict. Blocking the IPs and closing the alert skips investigation entirely and may block legitimate VPN exit nodes used by many other users. Lowering detection sensitivity suppresses future alerts rather than investigating the current one.
